title: probe-lifecycle-and-annotation-economics-playbook-2026
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This playbook describes the lifecycle, scheduling, and cost-accounting model for evaluation probes used across Redwood's eval harness. It combines operational rules, annotation economics, automated retirement policies, and quantization-aware handling to help teams run targeted, repeatable probes while keeping cost and label quality under control.

Audience
- ML engineers and evaluators who author/maintain probes
- Platform engineers who operate the eval scheduler and probe runner
- Product owners who require cost and coverage reporting

Scope
This document covers:
- Probe life stages (authoring → active → stale → retired)
- Annotation budgeting and pay rates, including SLA expectations for human review
- Scheduling windows, priority tiers, and run quotas
- Cost model: compute + annotation + storage attribution
- Quantization and model-variant sensitivity experiments for probes
- Automated triage signals and handoff to regression teams

1) Definitions
- Probe: A single, repeatable evaluation workload unit (prompt + expected checks + metadata).
- Probe Bundle: A logical group of probes used to exercise a slice (e.g., long-context, safety, coherence).
- Run: One execution of a probe against a target model/version with a specific config.
- Annotator Task: Human-labeling task derived from probe output for quality measurement.

2) Probe lifecycle (authoring to retirement)
- Authoring: Create probe with complete metadata (owner, business-impact, weight, tags, target-matrix). Use the probe template below.
- Review: 1 asynchronous reviewer + auto-lint. Criteria: reproducibility, determinism seed, clear pass/fail checks.
- Activation: Mark probe active and assign schedule tier (real-time / daily / weekly / monthly).
- Monitoring: Track run success rate, variance, token-cost, and annotation disagreement.
- Aging: If a probe has not triggered an annotator task and has <1% coverage drift for 90 days, it transitions to stale.
- Retirement: Owner or probe-committee retires the probe after stakeholder sign-off. Store archived probe with retention tags for 18 months.

3) Probe metadata template (YAML)
- For authoring, include the following fields in the probe manifest (example):

---
probe_id: "projX_longcontext_042"
owner: "team-language-infra"
business_impact: "high"
slice_tags: ["long-context", "kv-cache-sensitive"]
weight: 2
priority_tier: "daily"  # one of real-time/daily/weekly/monthly
seedable: true
expected_checks:
  - check_type: "semantic_equivalence"
    threshold: 0.82
run_configs:
  - model_family: "redwood-7b-opt"
    quant_profile: "int8-ev"
    context_length: 4096
---

4) Scheduling and quotas
- Priority tiers and default run quotas per probe bundle:
  - real-time: max 2 runs/minute, 95% of requests < 100ms scheduling latency
  - daily: up to 2,000 runs/day per bundle
  - weekly: up to 10,000 runs/week per bundle
  - monthly: up to 100,000 runs/month per bundle
- Backpressure policy: If aggregate queue latency > 5s for 3 consecutive minutes, degrade monthly → weekly → daily runs by 50% until recovery.

5) Annotation economics and budgeting
- Cost components per probe run: compute_cost + storage_cost + expected_annotation_cost*annotation_probability. Annotation probability is determined by sampling rate and sentinel triggers.
- Default annotation sampler: stratified sample 2% of runs for high-impact probes, 0.2% for low-impact. Increase sampling when variance > 0.05 (normalized score).
- Annotator pay bands (example internal rates):
  - QA/Junior annotator: $0.18 / labeled item
  - Senior annotator / adjudicator: $0.45 / disputed item
  - Specialist (safety/legal): $1.25 / review when escalated
- Budget allocation formula (string version):
  - monthly_annotation_budget = sum_over_probes(estimated_monthly_runs * sample_rate * pay_rate)
- Example: 10k runs/month * 2% sample * $0.18 = $36/month for that probe bundle.

6) Quality guardrails and thresholds
- Primary metrics to monitor per probe: pass_rate, semantic_similarity_mean, token_cost_per_run, annotator_disagreement_rate.
- Alert triggers (auto-created):
  - Pass rate drop > 6% absolute within 48h → create incident in eval-oncall (severity P2).
  - Annotator disagreement > 12% for two consecutive sample windows → escalate to triage board.
  - Token cost increase > 30% vs rolling-14d median → cost-owner notification.

7) Quantization-aware probe handling
- When evaluating quantized model variants, tag the probe run with quant_profile and track delta metrics (degradation vectors): semantic drift, hallucination-likelihood, latency delta.
- If semantic_similarity_mean drops by > 0.04 vs float baseline for > 5% of run samples, automatically flag for targeted re-annotation.
- Recommended experiment pattern: shadow-run quantized variant alongside float baseline with 5x sample multiplier on corner-case probes for first 72h.

8) Automated triage signals and handoff
- Triage signals (generated by telemetry pipeline): sudden pass_rate drop, sample variance spike, annotator disagreement, cross-slice correlation with infra incidents.
- Triage flow (automated):
  1. Signal detected → create Triage Issue in "eval-triage" board with prefilled diagnostics (probe_id, model_version, run_config, recent diff, telemetry links).
  2. On-call evaluator ACKS within 60 minutes.
  3. If not ACKed, escalate to ML infra oncall.
  4. If confirmed regression, create regression-bisect job and assign to regression team.

9) Regression bisect integration checklist
- Minimum reproducer: probe manifest + deterministic seed + model binary or docker tag + config file.
- Attach logs: token-level outputs, top-k logits (if enabled), KV cache metrics, latency breakdown.
- Run the automated-bisect command (example):

redwood-eval bisect --probe projX_longcontext_042 --from v2026-01-20 --to v2026-02-10 --output /tmp/bisect-report.json

10) Ownership and escalation matrix
- Probe owner: maintains manifest, signs off on retirement, first responder for probe-level failures.
- Eval oncall: responsible for triage and first-pass investigation (1-hour SLA).
- Regression squad: owns bisect and patching if code/model regression identified (72h remediation target for P1 regressions).
- Platform cost team: monthly reconciliation of annotation and compute spend vs budget.

11) Reporting and dashboards (minimum set)
- Probe Health dashboard (by bundle): pass_rate, sample_rate, annotator_disagreement, avg_token_cost, run_count_7d.
- Cost attribution table: probe_id → compute_cost_last_30d → annotation_cost_last_30d → total_cost.
- Freshness table: last_run, last_annotation, days_since_last_success.

12) Operational recipes (how-to)
- Author a new probe:
  1. Fork probe-template.yaml in the probe repo.
  2. Populate metadata and smoke-tests.
  3. Submit PR; include 1 reviewer and 1 cross-team reviewer if business_impact==high.
  4. Merge and mark active via the console tag.

- Increase sampling temporarily for a suspect model: CLI example:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
    -d '{"probe_bundle":"projX-longcontext","sample_multiplier":5, "reason":"quant-experiment-2026-02"}' 
    https://console.internal.redwood/api/eval/sample-control

- Archive a stale probe:
  1. Owner files retirement request.
  2. Probe committee reviews.
  3. If approved, set status: retired and set retention=18 months.

13) Cost-saving heuristics and knobs
- Apply cache-aware downsampling for probes that drive redundant KV cache fills.
- Use lower-fidelity quant probes (int8) for daily health checks, reserve float runs for weekly deep checks.
- Promote probe weights to reduce unnecessary runs: increase weight on high-value probes and reduce frequency for low-impact ones.

14) Example SQL for monthly annotation budget report (string):
SELECT probe_id, SUM(runs) as runs_30d, AVG(sample_rate) as avg_sample, SUM(sample_rate * runs * pay_rate) as est_annotation_cost FROM probe_runs WHERE run_ts > now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY probe_id ORDER BY est_annotation_cost DESC;

15) Appendices
A. Probe health SLA table:
- Active probes: scheduling latency p95 < 2s, run success rate > 98%
- Annotation turnaround: 95% labeled within 48 hours for sampled items
- Triage ACK: 60 minutes

B. Retention and privacy notes:
- Probes labeled as containing PII must use the privacy-redaction pipeline before any human annotation. See privacy-and-dp guidelines.
- Archive only non-sensitive artifacts; sensitive outputs must be purged after 90 days unless retained for a legal hold.

C. Contacts
- Probe platform owner: infra-probe-owners@redwood.ai
- Eval oncall rotation: eval-oncall@redwood.ai
- Annotation ops: annotation-ops@redwood.ai
